title: finding(tooling): 21 packages declare a react-dom peer no file in them consumes — the convention needs a decision, not a gate
body:
Split out of objectui#8198, which landed `pnpm check:unused-deps`. That gate judges `dependencies` and `optionalDependencies`; it deliberately does NOT judge `peerDependencies`, and this card is the decision it deferred.

Notation note: this body spells placeholders as WORDS rather than in their real angle-bracket form, because this repository has measured that GitHub's body sanitizer deletes tag-shaped fragments even inside backticks.

## Measured

On `fc32921aa`, with the same scanner the gate uses (module specifiers anywhere in the package, plus stylesheet at-rules, plus the `@types/X` follows X rule), **22 peer declarations have no consumer in the package that declares them** — and 21 of them are the same name:

| package | peer with no consumer |
|:--|:--|
| `app-shell`, `components`, `fields`, `layout`, `plugin-ai`, `plugin-calendar`, `plugin-charts`, `plugin-dashboard`, `plugin-designer`, `plugin-detail`, `plugin-editor`, `plugin-form`, `plugin-kanban`, `plugin-list`, `plugin-map`, `plugin-report`, `plugin-timeline`, `plugin-tree`, `plugin-view`, `providers`, `react` | `react-dom` |
| `app-shell` | `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` |

The count is printed by `pnpm check:unused-deps` on every run, so it cannot silently drift out of view.

## Why the gate does not judge it, and what the question actually is

A peer is a constraint on the HOST's graph, not a claim that this package imports the name. `react-dom` declared by a component library is a legitimate statement — "whatever application mounts me must have a DOM renderer" — even with zero imports. So `no importer` is simply not the right predicate for this field, and gating it would have turned 21 packages red on day one over a convention.

But the convention is worth an explicit decision, because it is not free and it is not uniform:

- **It is not free.** npm 7+ installs peers automatically. A peer nobody needs is still a download.
- **It is not uniform.** Three packages (`plugin-charts`, `plugin-form`, `plugin-list`) declare `react-dom` NOWHERE else — peer only. Two others (`layout`, `plugin-dashboard`) carried it in `dependencies` at an exact pin as well; objectui#8198 removed those two entries.
- **Some of these packages may genuinely need it.** Anything using `createPortal` does. The measurement above says nothing about that — it says only that no file in these packages NAMES `react-dom` today.

## The decision this card asks for

Pick one and write it down where the next author will read it:

1. **Keep it as a convention** — every renderable `@object-ui/*` package declares `react-dom` as a peer whether or not it imports it, because it is unmountable without one. Then say so in AGENTS.md section 3 and let the gate keep reporting the count as informational.
2. **Declare it only where it is used** — remove the 21 and let the three or four that actually reach `react-dom` (directly or through a portal) keep it. Smaller install graph, but a per-package audit.

Related: objectui#8059 (the doc-snippet root bound and peer-declared specifiers) is adjacent but distinct — it is about that gate's remedy text, not about which packages declare the peer.

Filed unassigned by the objectui#8198 implementation session; the measurement above is reproducible with `pnpm check:unused-deps`, whose summary line prints the peer count.
